hitl_conditions: Humans exit the driving loop but stay outside it: safety engineers supply 2022-2025 incident data, set speed and geofence constraints, interpret the twin's risk maps, and keep calibrating; the deployment decision remains human.
key_finding: A GIS/CAD digital twin of a 7000 m2 Czech automotive warehouse simulated replacing forklifts with three AMRs: risk scores fell ~40%, transport cycle time 28%, human-vehicle conflict zones 42%. All figures are simulated; AMRs are not deployed and the 'machine learning' is never specified.

quotes.text: Using the digital twin of the warehouse (created via GIS software and CAD imports), we conducted simulations to assess: Optimal AMR paths for material transport, Zones of high human-robot interaction (shared working space)
quotes.section: Materials and Methods, IV. Case Study Application, 2. Simulation Goals and Methodology (PDF p.4 = journal p.218)

quotes.text: The selected facility is a 7000 m2 warehouse that supports a production plant manufacturing automotive component. Its internal logistics process involves material movement between receiving docks, storage zones, production lines, and dispatch areas.
quotes.section: Materials and Methods, IV. Case Study Application, 1. Operational Scenario and Layout (PDF p.3 = journal p.217)

quotes.text: Following SGEM recommendations, the simulation incorporated multiple AI-driven control systems, allowing for adaptive decision-making: Path Planning Algorithms: Dynamic shortest-path calculation using A*, D*, and probabilistic roadmaps adapted to real-time sensor feedback
quotes.section: Materials and Methods, II. AI Algorithms Integrated into AMR Simulation (PDF p.3 = journal p.217)

quotes.text: Moreover, in high-traffic simulations, the system's machine learning algorithms adapted routing to avoid repeat exposure to dynamic hazard zones - such as unloading zones with manual pallet jacks.
quotes.section: Materials and Methods, IV. Case Study Application, 3. Key Outcomes (PDF p.4 = journal p.218)

quotes.text: Ergonomic risk mapping identified zones with historically high injury rates, primarily linked to manual pallet handling, tight-space forklift maneuvering, and prolonged seated driving with repetitive neck-torso motion - all tasks targeted for full automation by AMRs.
quotes.section: Results, II. Ergonomics and Human-Robot Interaction Improvements (PDF p.5 = journal p.219)

quotes.text: Human-Robot Interaction (HRI) protocols, including controlled speed, transparent motion, and multimodal safety alerts, contributed to safer shared workspaces and improved operator trust
